arxiv-1902-08695.creator: Jim Bryan
arxiv-1902-08695.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jim Bryan. A banana manifold is a compact Calabi-Yau threefold, fibered by Abelian surfaces, whose singular fibers have a singular locus given by a “banana configuration of curves”. A basic example is given by X 𝖻𝖺𝗇 := Bl Δ ⁡ ( S × ℙ 1 S ) X_{\mathsf{ban}}:=\operatorname{Bl}_{\Delta}(S\times_{{\mathbb{P}}^{1}}S) , the blowup along the diagonal of the fibered product of a generic rational elliptic surface S → ℙ 1 S\to{\mathbb{P}}^{1} with itself.

arxiv-2103-03148.title: Orbital Hall effect as an alternative to valley Hall effect in gapped graphene
arxiv-2103-03148.creator: Sayantika Bhowal, Giovanni Vignale
arxiv-2103-03148.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sayantika Bhowal, Giovanni Vignale. Gapped graphene has been proposed to be a good platform to observe the valley Hall effect, a transport phenomenon involving the flow of electrons that are characterized by different valley indices. In the present work, we show that this phenomenon is better described as an instance of the orbital Hall effect, where the ambiguous “valley” indices are replaced by a physical quantity, the orbital magnetic moment, which can be defined uniformly over the entire Brillouin zone.

arxiv-2312-02107.title: Pair filamentation and laser scattering in beam-driven QED cascades
arxiv-2312-02107.creator: Kenan Qu, Alec Griffith, Nathaniel J. Fisch
arxiv-2312-02107.description: Abstract We report the observation of longitudinal filamentation of an electron-positron pair plasma in a beam-driven QED cascade. The filaments are created in the “pair-reflection” regime, where the generated pairs are partially stopped and reflected in the strong laser field. The density filaments form near the center of the laser pulse and have diameters similar to the laser wavelength.

arxiv-2405-05552.title: Bidirectional Progressive Transformer for Interaction Intention Anticipation
arxiv-2405-05552.creator: Zichen Zhang, Hongchen Luo, Wei Zhai, Yang Cao, Yu Kang
arxiv-2405-05552.description: Abstract † † *Corresponding Author. Interaction intention anticipation aims to jointly predict future hand trajectories and interaction hotspots. Existing research often treated trajectory forecasting and interaction hotspots prediction as separate tasks or solely considered the impact of trajectories on interaction hotspots, which led to the accumulation of prediction errors over time.

arxiv-2409-07334.title: Blow-up analysis and degree theory for the Webster curvature prescription problem in three dimensions
arxiv-2409-07334.creator: Claudio Afeltra
arxiv-2409-07334.description: Abstract Given a strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold M M of dimension three and positive CR Yamabe class, and a positive smooth function K : M → 𝐑 K:M\to\mathbf{R} verifying some mild and generic hypotheses, we prove the compactness of the set of solutions of the Webster curvature prescription problem associated to K K , and we compute the Leray-Schauder degree

arxiv-2505-20776.title: SpecExtend : A Drop-in Enhancement for Speculative Decoding of Long Sequences
arxiv-2505-20776.creator: Jungyoub Cha, Hyunjong Kim, Sungzoon Cho
arxiv-2505-20776.description: Abstract Speculative decoding is a widely adopted technique for accelerating inference in large language models (LLMs), but its performance degrades on long inputs due to increased attention cost and reduced draft accuracy. We introduce SpecExtend, a drop-in enhancement that improves the performance of speculative decoding on long sequences without any additional training.

arxiv-2507-07113.title: Sampled Grid Pairwise Likelihood (SG-PL): An Efficient Approach for Spatial Regression on Large Data
arxiv-2507-07113.creator: Giuseppe Arbia, Vincenzo Nardelli, Niccolò Salvini
arxiv-2507-07113.description: Abstract Estimating spatial regression models on large, irregularly structured datasets poses significant computational hurdles. While Pairwise Likelihood (PL) methods offer a pathway to simplify these estimations, the efficient selection of informative observation pairs remains a critical challenge, particularly as data volume and complexity grow.

arxiv-2507-11240.title: Optimal Sensor Scheduling and Selection for Continuous-Discrete Kalman Filtering with Auxiliary Dynamics
arxiv-2507-11240.creator: Mohamad Al Ahdab, John Leth, Zheng-Hua Tan
arxiv-2507-11240.description: Abstract We study the Continuous-Discrete Kalman Filter (CD-KF) for State-Space Models (SSMs) where continuous-time dynamics are observed via multiple sensors with discrete, irregularly timed measurements. Our focus extends to scenarios in which the measurement process is coupled with the states of an auxiliary SSM.

europmc-pmc4824800.title: Alkaline Phosphatase and Hypophosphatasia.
europmc-pmc4824800.creator: Millán JL, Whyte MP.
europmc-pmc4824800.description: Hypophosphatasia (HPP) results from ALPL mutations leading to deficient activity of the tissue-non-specific alkaline phosphatase isozyme (TNAP) and thereby extracellular accumulation of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi), a natural substrate of TNAP and potent inhibitor of...

plos-pone-0354796.title: Sex differences in social cognition: Insights from a sample enriched for social dysfunction
plos-pone-0354796.creator: Kathryn C Kemp, Scott D Blain, Saba Zehra, Serena DeStefani, Laura Locarno, Kelly Mathis, Carly A Lasagna, Costanza Colombi
plos-pone-0354796.description: Sex differences in social cognition: Insights from a sample enriched for social dysfunction

pmc-10518750.title: Top‐down effects of filter‐feeding fish and bivalves moderate bottom‐up effects of nutrients on phytoplankton in subtropical shallow lakes: An outdoor mesocosm study
pmc-10518750.creator: You Zhang, Ruijie Shen, Kuanyi Li, Qisheng Li, Huihui Chen, Hu He, Xiaohong Gu, Zhigang Mao, Richard K Johnson
pmc-10518750.description: Biomanipulation has been widely used in the ecological restoration of eutrophic lakes for decades. However, biomanipulation is prone to failure if external nutrient loads are not reduced. In order to explore the importance of filter‐feeding fish and bivalves on algal control, an outdoor mesocosm experiment was conducted using different nutrient concentrations.

pmc-11355758.title: Reduction in Ochratoxin A Occurrence in Coffee: From Good Practices to Biocontrol Agents
pmc-11355758.creator: Claudia López-Rodríguez, Carol Verheecke-Vaessen, Caroline Strub, Angélique Fontana, Sabine Schorr-Galindo, Angel Medina
pmc-11355758.description: Ochratoxin A (OTA) is a mycotoxin mainly produced by Aspergillus section Circumdati and section Nigri across the coffee chain. OTA is nephrotoxic and is a threat to human health. This review summarizes current knowledge on how to reduce OTA concentration in coffee from farm to cup.

pmc-11740792.title: Delivering national immunisation programmes – a blanket opportunity for the pharmacy profession or a case of horses for courses?
pmc-11740792.creator: Christina Wilson
pmc-11740792.description: This opinion piece explores the opportunities and challenges from increased utilisation of pharmacists and pharmacy technicians in delivery of the UK immunisation programme, within the recent legislative change enabling pharmacy technicians to administer Prescription Only Medicines (POMs) under Patient Group Directions (PGDs).

pmc-12555993.title: Empowering Children: Co-Design Boosts Health Literacy and Learning Outcomes in primary school
pmc-12555993.creator: W van Boxtel, K Jerković-Ćosić, M ChinAPaw
pmc-12555993.description: BackgroundResearch underscores the primary school's pivotal role in educating children on managing health information. To enhance the effectiveness of interventions, relevance for the children and engagement of children in learning activities co-design is a promising participatory method. It fosters empowerment and ownership among young learners which is needed for active involvement in learning health literacy (HL) skills.

pmc-12656135.title: Aflatoxins in Mexican Maize Systems: From Genetic Resources to Agroecological Resilience and Co-Occurrence with Fumonisins
pmc-12656135.creator: Carlos Muñoz-Zavala, Obed Solís-Martínez, Jessica Berenice Valencia-Luna, Kai Sonder, Ana María Hernández-Anguiano, Natalia Palacios-Rojas
pmc-12656135.description: Aflatoxins (AFs) and fumonisins (FUMs) are among the most prevalent and toxic mycotoxins affecting maize production globally. In Mexico, their co-occurrence poses a significant public health concern, as maize is not only a dietary staple but also predominantly grown and consumed at the household level.

pmc-12835017.title: Distribution and human health risk of polychlorinated biphenyls in soil and plants in Koko Town, Delta State, Nigeria
pmc-12835017.creator: Amaka Michael, Abraham O Ekperusi, Ndu P Okeke, Anthonia E Gbuvboro
pmc-12835017.description: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) remain a global concern due to their environmental persistence and toxicity. However, their distribution in industrial and residential areas in Nigeria is insufficiently documented. This study investigated PCB concentrations in soils and commonly consumed plants from five sites around industrial areas in Koko Town, Delta State.

pmc-12952224.title: Distinct Antibody Fc-profiles in Lymph During Homeostasis and Chronic HIV Infection
pmc-12952224.creator: Ryan P McNamara, Audrey L Butler, Sepideh Dolatshahi, Sabian Taylor, Yoav Dori, Ian Frank, Maxim G Itkin, Michael R Betts, Galit Alter
pmc-12952224.description: Background:Antibodies play a critical role in the control of pathogens and tumors through their ability to recognize non-self and then direct immune-mediated destruction. Antibodies are generated by plasma cells or plasmablasts, located throughout the tissues, and are transported between blood, lymph, mucosal secretions, and tissues to survey all sites for pathogens or malignant cells.

pmc-13115178.title: Optimizing Workflow, Safety and Children’s Comfort in the Operating Theatre: A Mixed-Method Study Exploring Nurses’ and Caregivers’ Experiences and Possible Areas for Improvement
pmc-13115178.creator: Raffaella Dobrina, Silvana Schreiber, Andrea Cassone, Paola Di Rocco, Valentina Cvetkovic, Martina Debelli, Giulia Galvani, Lucio Torelli, Loreto Lancia, Angelo Dante, Benedetta Tagliapietra
pmc-13115178.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Caregivers rated their OT experience more positively than nurses did.Late education in the OT limits caregivers’ ability to support children. What are the implications of the main findings? Early, clear information helps caregivers reduce child anxiety during induction.Calm, informed caregivers improve safety and workflow in the OT.

pmc-13225886.title: Does time heal all wounds? Examining the lasting impact of historic redlining on contemporary racial disparities in allostatic load in Baltimore, Maryland
pmc-13225886.creator: Marcus R Andrews, Linda M Chatters, Roshanak Mehdipanah, Andrew Grogan-Kaylor, Michele K Evans, Alan B Zonderman, Tiffany M Powell-Wiley, Amy J Schulz
pmc-13225886.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective:To examine associations between historical residential redlining, a form of institutional racism, and contemporary allostatic load (AL), an indicator of physiologic stress, examine differences by race, and whether associations are mediated by neighborhood deprivation.Methods:We used data from Wave 4 (2013–2017) of the Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS) study in Baltimore, MD, Home Owners Loan Corporation (HOLC) scores, and data from the American Community Survey (ACS).

pmc-13291889.title: A Novel Sarcopenia Screening Score Based on Thyroid Function Parameters in Euthyroid Middle‐Aged and Elderly Chinese Adults
pmc-13291889.creator: Fei Ding, Jirong Yue, Yong He

pmc-13377701.title: Anesthetic management of hip fracture surgery in a patient with concurrent cardio-cerebral infarction: a case report
pmc-13377701.creator: Caifeng Wang, Yuxin Wang, Xiang Xue, Xinxin Wang, Yujie Li, Zhou Zhou, Xiaobao Zhang
pmc-13377701.description: RationaleCardio-Cerebral Infarction (CCI), defined by the simultaneous occurrence of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS), is a rare clinical entity associated with high mortality. Currently, no consensus exists regarding its optimal management strategy or the timing of surgical intervention.Patient’s concernsWe present the case of a 79-year-old female admitted for a hip fracture who subsequently developed Cardio-Cerebral Infarction.

pmc-13448166.title: Incidence, Etiologies, and Outcomes of Respiratory Distress in Newborns Admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital in Rural South-West Bihar
pmc-13448166.creator: Richa Raj, Neha Kumari, Om Prakash Singh, Mani Kant Kumar
pmc-13448166.description: BackgroundOne of the most frequent reasons for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) hospitalization is respiratory distress, which causes significant early neonatal morbidity and mortality, especially in resource-constrained environments. Etiology and related risk factors need to be identified early to enhance the outcome of neonates.

pmc-13578319.title: A machine learning framework for multimodal temporal prediction of neurological outcome after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
pmc-13578319.creator: Jee Yong Lim, Han Joon Kim
